title: Fading Support for Korean Unification: Cohort Persistence and Labour-Market Competition
meta: with Youngshin Cho (Bank of Korea) and Kyoochul Kim (Ewha Womans University) · Draft presented at a Bank of Korea seminar, 2026
description: The share of South Koreans who regard unification as necessary has fallen below half. This decline is often attributed to younger generations, while economic opposition is commonly framed around fiscal costs and tax burdens. Using 19 waves of the Unification Perception Survey (2007–2025), this study constructs a pseudo-panel of seven birth cohorts and examines differences across education and occupation. Later-born cohorts are less supportive at comparable ages, with little evidence that these gaps narrow as they age. Yet support also declined over time within younger and older cohorts alike, accounting for about half of the overall decline. More-educated respondents are more supportive, while workers in low-skilled occupations are less so. The occupational gap is concentrated at prime working age and is not evident among older workers. Together, these findings qualify youth-centred accounts of declining support and extend fiscal-cost explanations by suggesting labour-market competition as another potential source of opposition.

title: The Long-Term Effects of the 1990s North Korean Famine on Health and Labor Market Outcomes
meta: with Jongmin Lee (Korea National Defense University)
description: Studies how early-life exposure to the 1990s North Korean famine affected the later-life health and labor-market outcomes of North Korean defectors. Using South Korea’s National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) data, the project compares famine-exposed cohorts with other defector cohorts and matched South Korean residents, with adult height as a proxy for early-life nutrition, and estimates effects on disease prevalence, employment, occupational status, and income.

title: Regional Economic Reconfiguration in Russia’s Far East and the Northern Korean Peninsula: Structural Implications of Deepening North Korea–China–Russia Cooperation
description: Examines how deepening cooperation among North Korea, China, and Russia is reshaping the regional economy of Russia’s Far East and the northern Korean Peninsula. Since the Russia–Ukraine war, Russia has turned more decisively toward East Asia while North Korea has strengthened its strategic and economic ties with Russia, with China remaining central to regional trade, logistics, and industrial networks. The project analyzes whether these developments are producing a new regional economic structure linking Russia’s Far East, Northeast China, and North Korea, focusing on logistics routes, industrial linkages, energy cooperation, labor mobility, and the strategic role of North Korea, and assesses the structural implications of trilateral cooperation for the future of the northern Korean Peninsula and South Korea’s northern economic strategy.

title: Health Assimilation among North Korean Defectors in South Korea
meta: with Jongmin Lee (Korea National Defense University)
description: Analyzes how the health status of North Korean defectors changes after resettlement in South Korea, using NHIS administrative data from 2002 to 2024. Compares defectors with matched South Korean residents on chronic diseases, mental health, biomarkers, and health behaviors, and examines whether health gaps narrow or widen over time and across local socioeconomic conditions.
